info.title: Enterprise Forms Authorization Authority (INTERNAL)
info.description: Private contract. Reachable only over the authority network path with the workload credential and a delegated user assertion. Not part of the browser-facing API.

get.summary: Ready only when the signing provider, authority store, SpiceDB schema and independent archive are all usable.

post.summary: Authoritative permission check at the authority-held projection token; fails closed while the organization gate is closed.
Authority-sourced discoverable record ids (registered + discover permission); never derived from business tables.

get.summary: Authoritative designers and create-record principals of a form; fails closed while the organization gate is closed.

post.summary: Validated, idempotent, revision-bound security mutation. 202 means committed, not effective; poll until Effective.

AC-9 (reconciler credential only): read-only outcome of one AddTeamMember/RemoveTeamMember command bound by (organization, idempotency key, allowlisted kind), with the organization's revisions and the effective membership of the command's own (team, member) pair at the projection-applied revision. Uniform found=false for unknown organization, key or kind mismatch; membership null when rejected or quarantined. No lock, revision, journal or SpiceDB access.

Phase C7 M4 (verifier only): every current field protection decision of the organization (Authority protection resources, never the business form list) with its latest attestation; organization-complete only when each decision has a complete attestation under that decision.

Validates the exact candidate snapshot against the accepted head and the actor's edit scope (or, without a user, the reprotection rules of an effective PublishFormSecurityRevision command), then signs it. Not a generic signing endpoint.
Proves the staged bytes equal the approved candidate and CAS-advances the trusted content head.

get.summary: AC-1: accepted content revisions of a record (ascending, cursor by revision, at most 100 per page) from the Authority's own rows: revision, accepted time, actor or protection-migration attribution, key version and whether it is still verifiable. Full read of the record now is required (concealment-safe 404 otherwise). Read-only; no row content and no signature work.

post.summary: Compares the observed staged items with the complete accepted leaf index, verifies every signature and the root, and returns the authorized subset.

Phase C7 OD-6: batch of 1..50 records, each verified exactly like VerifyRecordProjection (registry, discover/read, quarantine, archive receipt, complete leaf set, every signature, root, readable field scope) against the head the caller expects. Per-record typed results; mismatches quarantine the record; read action only. Not a signature oracle: every record needs the caller's own read or discover permission.

AC-5: the registered records of one form (registry parent) that the delegated user may discover, each with its accepted head, fixed as an Authority-held snapshot at one authorization, projection and content revision. More eligible records than maximum_entries ⇒ 422 LIMIT_EXCEEDED with no entries. Quarantined heads and resources are listed with their flag (a trusted search over them must fail).

Validates the caller's own snapshot against current Authority state: expiry, gate, authorization and projection revision (any change invalidates, OD-5), and — when the organization's content revision moved — every entry's head, quarantine and registry state. The id alone proves nothing.
Phase C7 M3 (OD-8): journals one field-search execution over the caller's own snapshot on the audit stream (field ids, operators, counts, outcome, duration — never predicate values or record ids).

OD-1 (verifier workload only): the complete registered population of the form scoped by an effective PublishFormSecurityRevision command — records no user can discover included — with heads, quarantine and registry state, as a paged Authority-held snapshot. Issuance and denials are journaled on the audit stream. Never routed through the business API.

get.summary: A further page of the verifier's own migration catalogue snapshot (409 after expiry).

post.summary: Validates the verifier's snapshot like the user snapshot, plus that the scoping command is still the field's current protection decision.

Phase C7 M4 (G19, verifier only): verifies 1..50 entries of the verifier's own snapshot against their accepted manifests (complete leaf set, every HMAC, root, archive receipt; tampering quarantines the head) and counts the decision's field rows in the old and the target form from the verified bytes. Counts only — never contents. A census held for the same accepted operation is reused only when it was verified since reuseSinceSnapshotId (this reconciliation's first snapshot) was issued; anything else is re-verified.

Phase C7 M4 (G19, verifier only): the Authority's reconciliation report for the snapshot's protection decision, computed now under the organization lock from the registry population, current heads and census results (nothing from the business database), journaled on the audit stream before it is returned. 409 when the decision was superseded.
Provisions organization state, identity bindings, organization roles and the organization integrity key (Stage A stand-in for the PIM/dual-control workflow).

get.summary: Operator view: the organization's verified members and Security Administrators (identities only), and whether dual-controlled approval is available here.

post.summary: DR-C7-3: first Security Administrator of an organization with none usable. dry_run previews the exact change and the statement to approve; execution needs two ES256 approvals from distinct registered approvers (OPERATOR_DUAL_CONTROL_UNAVAILABLE where approvals are not available, e.g. staging/production). Single-use operation id; journaled and alerted.

DR-C7-3: recovery when the organization's Security Administrators are unavailable. Incident reference required; explicit scope (one appointee, named administrators removed); two independent approvals; critical security alert; journaled.

AC-7.4: dry run, then two ES256 approvals from distinct registered approvers over the exact statement (Development/Testing only until PIM). Re-checks request state, expiry, the requesting owner, the identity and its issuer inside the organization lock; creates the identity binding (and optional designer role) as one journaled command.

Recovery ceremony: registers new Platform Operator identities only while fewer than two are active. Dry run first; execution needs two ES256 custodian approvals (DR-C7-3 keys) over the statement. Critical alert; platform journal.
After a database restore: re-applies archived platform events beyond the database head, each verified against the chain; quarantines on mismatch. Never chooses or edits state.
Testing only: arms a one-shot process crash at a named protocol transition (SEC-P09).

get.summary: Testing only: armed fault and number of operations held at a pause point.

post.summary: Testing only: turns field-scoped contributor writes on or off for the disposable integration stack (Phase C5, D10); null restores the deployment configuration.

get.summary: The signed-in Platform Operator, their four platform permissions and the platform journal state.
platform.operators.view: every registered operator (identity and status) and pending two-operator proposals.

post.summary: platform.operators.manage: propose Provision, Reinstate or Remove (dry run returns the statement). A different active operator, not the target, must confirm.
Emergency suspension by one active operator (self included): immediate, invalidates the target's pending approvals, alerted.
platform.membership_requests.review: cross-organization request metadata, newest first, 15 per page by default (opaque cursor bound to the operator and filter).

get.summary: Request metadata, the exact statement v2 and its SHA-256, recorded approvals and the caller's eligibility. The view is journaled.

post.summary: platform.membership_requests.decide: one operator's approval. The first is stored as pending evidence; a valid second approval by a different operator creates the membership atomically.
The approving operator withdraws their own pending approval (nobody else can).
One operator rejects with a justification and evidence; any pending approval is invalidated; nothing is granted.

Create an immutable onboarding request (dry run validates). The Authority generates the organization id and every owner's user id; 2-10 owners from one approved issuer, never a Platform Operator identity.
Onboarding requests, newest first, 15 per page by default (opaque cursor bound to the operator and filter).

get.summary: The request, its frozen statement and SHA-256, owners, approvals, key custody status, activation and the caller's eligibility.

post.summary: Organizations with lifecycle and owner, Security Administrator and member counts only (metadata; no records, documents, teams or shares).

get.summary: Owner identities, counts and onboarding provenance. The view is audited on the organization's audit stream before it is returned.
Read-only, for the development key custody tool: the single key name an approved request needs and whether it may be provisioned now. The Authority never creates the key.

post.summary: Open an immutable owner recovery case (dry run validates) for an organization with fewer than two eligible owners. Grants nothing; three operators approve, then the waiting period runs.
Recovery cases, newest first, 15 per page by default (opaque cursor bound to the operator and filter).

get.summary: The case, its frozen statement and SHA-256, owners, evidence, approvals, waiting period, objection and the caller's eligibility. Audited on the organization's audit stream before it is returned.

post.summary: Members who may be proposed as replacement owners (enabled, not owners, not operator identities): minimum metadata, server-side filter and paging; audited before disclosure.
The organization's open recovery case for an enabled owner or Security Administrator (not found for anyone else).
Object to the open case (fresh step-up, explanation). Ends the case immediately; recorded in the platform journal and the organization's audit stream.
Registers the SHA-256 digest of a new session secret for the delegated user (bound identity required) and revokes the session it replaces.
Valid only when not revoked, within absolute and idle expiry, and bound to the same enabled identity. Never extends the absolute expiry.
Idempotent revocation by the session's own identity (sign-out).

Searchable fields of a form for the delegated user (query_fields + active AC-6 approvals; labels and options from the approval snapshot) and, for designers and security administrators only, the search configuration of the latest registered published version. Identical empty answer for no access and unknown forms.

Phase C7 M3: forms of the caller's organization with an Authority-registered published version (title, version, field and approval counts) for search-approval administration. administer_security only; no Designer or record access needed or granted.

The organization's Security Administrators (system_administrator) with their verified identities and appointing command; candidates (enabled identities) only for Security Administrators. Organization owners see the roster read-only; anyone else gets 404. Appointment and removal are GrantSystemRole / RevokeSystemRole security commands.

AC-7.3: every identity binding of the caller's organization with its enabled state and organization roles, two-owner proposals and membership requests of the last 30 days. Organization owners and Security Administrators only; anyone else gets 404. No record content or counts.
